experiment.description: Part 30. Naive fusion and V1 PrismFlow on LANL cyber1, at 300 s (computer, window) samples, days 1-16, split by TIME with a two-day gap. Run twice: WITH the auth view and WITHOUT it, because the red-team labels are drawn from auth data.

Part 30. Naive fusion and V1 PrismFlow on LANL cyber1, at 300 s (computer, window) samples, days 1-16, split by TIME with a two-day gap. Run twice: WITH the auth view and WITHOUT it, because the red-team labels are drawn from auth data.

label_meaning: A sample is (computer, 300 s window). attack = 1 means a redteam.txt.gz event in that window names that computer as its source or its destination. benign = 0 means NO KNOWN red-team event does, which is not the same as verified clean: the red-team file covers only the activity LANL's red team recorded, so an unlabelled compromise inside the capture is counted as benign here.

split_report.label_meaning: A sample is (computer, 300 s window). attack = 1 means a redteam.txt.gz event in that window names that computer as its source or its destination. benign = 0 means NO KNOWN red-team event does, which is not the same as verified clean: the red-team file covers only the activity LANL's red team recorded, so an unlabelled compromise inside the capture is counted as benign here.

estimated_population_cells_union.method: Not directly counted. The union over views of occupied cells cannot be derived from per-view counts, and counting it exactly would need a cross-view per-window set this loader does not keep. The exact per-view counts are in per_view; the union is bounded below by their maximum and above by their sum.

execution_mode.rule: Fixed before measuring: use parallel units if parallel throughput >= 2x run 1's sequential throughput, else sequential. Parallelism is across (arm, system, seed) units only; hyperparameters and seeds 0-4 are unchanged.
execution_mode.benchmark_note: 200 real training steps of a with_auth naive model on the real train block, 10 warm-up steps discarded. torch's default thread count (12) is 2.35x slower per step than 1 thread: tiny batches of a 4-view MLP spend more time in thread synchronisation than in arithmetic. Run 1 ran at the default and its measured 253 s/naive model matches this benchmark's 248 s projection at 12 threads, which is the check that the benchmark reflects reality.

benchmark_run2_contended.note: CONTAMINATED, not a clean benchmark. No PrismFlow process was running (all 22 orphans had been terminated), but this box carried 20-33% load from unrelated desktop applications throughout. The readings are non-monotonic in thread count and 12 threads alone spans 11.1-35.7 ms/step across three identical repeats, so this run cannot discriminate 1 from 2 from 4 threads. The one signal it reproduces is that 12 threads (torch's default here) is never faster and is sometimes 3x slower. The thread choice below was therefore taken from the 2026-10-17 idle-machine benchmark, which is the only clean one, and was fixed before this run's units were launched.

orphans_terminated_before_benchmark.detail: A Phase 2 scheduler from the earlier stopped session (scratchpad e346cb63, phase2.sh) was still live and had launched 11 units at 15:12:18, 4 minutes before this run began. Its 22 run_lanl.py processes were 11 units x (launcher stub + interpreter). The brief says to terminate processes whose command line shows run_lanl.py; the bash phase2.sh supervisors do not name run_lanl.py but hold an 11-slot queue over the remaining 29 units and would have relaunched every process killed, so they were stopped first. Nothing else was touched. No unit file from that scheduler had been written, so no result was discarded.

terminated: run_lanl.py --aggregate (2 processes, PID 9016 and 19268, started 15:40:22, still running 40 minutes later on a then-incomplete set of arms). Its command line shows run_lanl.py, its parent session was gone, and its output would have been superseded by the final aggregate, so it was terminated. Nothing it had written was kept.
phase0b_process_audit_run2_continuation.not_terminated: The other 22 processes were 11 live units of the Phase 2 scheduler (phase2.sh, supervisor PID 18016, started 15:22:36) working the brief's own arm priority order. They are NOT orphans: the supervisor shell was alive, the queue was advancing, and a 40-second CPU sample confirmed every one of them accumulating CPU time. Killing them would have discarded in-flight work on the arms the brief owes.
phase0b_process_audit_run2_continuation.cpu_not_idle_reading_taken: The brief's Phase 1 asks for a thread benchmark on an IDLE machine. The machine was NOT idle in this session and was not made idle, because idling it meant killing the owed arms mid-flight. The conservative reading taken, recorded here rather than resolved by asking: Phase 1 was already executed and committed before this session - the thread count and the parallel-vs-sequential decision were fixed from the 2026-10-17 idle-machine benchmark and had already been applied to every unit on disk - so repeating it could only have produced a second contaminated reading at the cost of the arms. No new benchmark was run in this session and no benchmark number here comes from a loaded box except the one already labelled CONTAMINATED and excluded.

thread_count_reproducibility_observation.status: REPORTED, NOT FIXED. Frozen-module observation; no frozen code was changed and no committed value was regenerated.
thread_count_reproducibility_observation.what: A committed Part 28 ENIV value is reproducible only at the torch thread count that produced it. tests/unit/test_ait_attack.py::test_clean_dependence_matches_part28 re-computes eniv_eigen and asserts it equals Part 28's committed seed-0 value to abs=1e-6.
thread_count_reproducibility_observation.why_it_matters_here: Part 30 run 1 ran at torch's default 12 threads and run 2 at 1 thread. The thread count changes the order in which sums are accumulated during training, so it changes the fitted weights and then every diagnostic computed from them. The difference is about 0.3% of ENIV on AIT - four orders of magnitude above the 1e-6 tolerance that test asserts - which is the scale to keep in mind when reading this Part's run-1-vs-run-2 replicate table and its seed-0 equivalence check. It is arithmetic, not a quality difference between the systems.
thread_count_reproducibility_observation.gate_consequence: The Part 30 gate test suite is therefore run at the DEFAULT thread count, which is the count the committed values were produced at. Under OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 that one test fails; that is the test detecting a thread change, not a defect introduced by Part 30.

achieved_parallel_measured.note: A unit takes LONGER in this mode than it did sequentially - 1769 s against run 1's 336 s - because 11 of them share the box. The gain is throughput, not latency. The projection above overstated that gain because it assumed no contention between concurrent units; the decision rule (at least 2x run 1's sequential throughput) is met on the MEASURED figure as well as the projected one, so the mode choice stands on what happened rather than on the forecast.

equivalence_check_seed0.note: Same seed, same hyperparameters, same sample table and the same time split. A non-zero difference here is execution mode and floating-point reduction order, not a different experiment: run 1 ran sequentially at torch's default 12 threads and run 2 at 1 thread, which changes the order in which sums are accumulated. The difference is NOT evidence about either system's quality.

part29_test_a_natural_attack_windows.note: ENIV and mean pairwise dependence on real attack vs real benign test windows. No synthetic perturbation. LANL's red-team file has no attack-step taxonomy, so unlike Part 29 on AIT there is no dnsteal-only/multi-step split; this is one attack population, not two pooled.

part29_tests_not_run.B_chorus_attack: NOT RUN. Part 29's grid is k in {1,2,3} x Part 09's epsilon and beta grid, retrained per cell, which does not fit this Part's time budget. No partial grid is reported, because a subset of the cells is not the test.
part29_tests_not_run.C_honest_duplication: PARTIALLY RUN. The strict same-sensor pair does not exist here: LANL cyber1 ships no sensor-group definition, so there is no within-group pair to score and the answer is NO EVIDENCE. The 'different sensors, naturally dependent' half needs the most/least dependent pairs, which ARE written to systems.<name>.pair_table; scoring the detector on them was not run.
part29_tests_not_run.D_missingness: NOT RUN as a detector-AUC test. Per-view missing fractions on train and test ARE measured above, and whole arms without flows and without dns ARE run, which is a stronger answer than masking at 30%/50%; but Part 10's masked detector AUC itself was not computed.

phase3_diagnostics.missing_view_handling: A missing view is carried as a BOOLEAN MASK, not as a zero-filled observation. `prismflow/statistics/dependence.py::feature_dependence_matrix` receives `view_mask` and `prismflow/statistics/dependence.py::available_views` reduces it to the per-view availability vector that `prismflow/eniv/eniv.py::compute_eniv` is given, so an absent view is excluded from the pair statistics rather than contributing a zero row. The feature row of an absent view IS zero in the tensor (`run_lanl.py::apply_scaler` leaves `views[~rows, v] = 0.0`), but the encoder never consumes it because `MultiViewEncoder` gates on the mask. Consequence for the pair table: a dns pair is computed over the samples where BOTH views of the pair are present, not over all samples, so the dns pairs rest on the ~2% of samples that have a dns record.

arm_coverage.note: Shared sample table: all arms use the SAME rows, labels and split. An arm drops a view's feature columns and encoder, never a row. A row with no present view among the arm's views is unpredictable by construction - all models score it identically.

trivial_baselines.note: Each row is a SINGLE SCALAR, no training. Orientation (sign) is chosen on the train block only and then applied unchanged to test.

host_audit.note: A computer with attack samples in BOTH blocks lets a model recognise the host rather than the behaviour, which is why the seen/unseen split below is reported.

seen_unseen.note: 'seen' = the attack sample's computer also has at least one attack sample in the train block. Each group is scored against all benign test samples. Descriptive, not a controlled comparison.

cluster_bootstrap.note: 2000 replicates, fixed seed 12345, clusters = test computers, paired (same resampled computers for both systems, every seed). Measures test-set sampling variability; the per-seed std measures training randomness. They are not interchangeable.

replicate_run1_vs_run2.note: Same seeds, same hyperparameters, same sample rule; run 1 ran sequentially at torch's default thread count, run 2 in this Part's chosen mode. Differences are execution mode and floating-point reduction order, not a different experiment.
